summary.intent: Resolve the merge conflict on PR #81 (held-out set), then continue with the bounded-work PRs, starting with rule 1: a fixed parse stack plus a nesting pre-scan for the TypeScript and Rust analyzers.
summary.outcome: The conflict in scripts/rg-compare.py was resolved and pushed to #81's branch (f78cf69, no force). just ci, the full harness and the benchmark subset all exit 0, and the gates were raised to 0.9. GitHub mergeability was not confirmed because the API timed out. The rule 1 parse-stack work was handed to an agent and is still running.

repo: The ADR's bounded-work plan is split into PRs. Rule 1 is the parse stack and nesting bound. The size-before-read gate and hit-text cap come next, then --timeout, then the CI scaling tests.

The parse-stack work touches analysis/ts/parse.rs and analysis/rust/. These files don't overlap #79, which edits text search, so it can proceed in parallel. The size-before-read gate and hit-text cap edit text search and must wait for #79 to merge.
scripts/rg-compare.py holds the harness constants. #77 reorganized them into a per-language structure, and the held-out branch adds a HELD_OUT marker on top of main's shared test-path rules.

Harness baselines after the merge: tuned set 58/59, 17/18 and 15/16; Rust on fd 22/24; held-out set 23/24 questions and 12/12 members. Gates for Rust, held-out questions and held-out members were raised from 0 to 0.9.
Decision-log entry §34 covers the held-out set, the Rust gate, and the rule that held-out misses are never fixed by editing the question.
The old ~254 KiB TypeScript size cap came from stack limits. A 3.4 MB generated TypeScript file currently returns `search: []`.
The nesting pre-scan must over-estimate nesting, never under-estimate. A wrong guess upward only skips a useless file, but a guess downward can crash the process.

code.finding: The only conflicted file in the #81 merge. Resolved by keeping main's shared test-path rules from #77's per-language structure together with this branch's HELD_OUT marker.

workflow: Verify results by exit code (just ci, harness, benchmark subset) rather than by reading output.
Push to a PR branch without force after resolving a merge conflict.

Delegate measurement-heavy work to an agent. The brief specifies measuring first with a throwaway experiment, a 2x safety factor, and explicit pass criteria, including a byte-for-byte binary comparison on at least 60 queries.
Put the gate changes and the decision-log entry in the same PR, which avoids a follow-up PR.

friction: The GitHub API timed out twice with a TLS handshake error, so PR #81's mergeability after the push could not be confirmed.
Entire Gates on the open PRs are waiting on user approval.
open_items: Confirm that PR #81 now reads as mergeable on GitHub.
Wait for the rule 1 parse-stack agent to finish: measure stack bytes per nesting level, set constants, add the pre-scan, replace the size cap, and conditionally drop the Rust leak workaround.
After #79 merges: the size-before-read gate and the hit-text cap.
Then add --timeout and the CI scaling tests.
Open PRs #81, #79 and release PR #59 are awaiting approval on Entire Gates.
